name: PhosphorIconLibrary
description: Rules for the Phosphor icon library, an alternative to Lucide (IconLibrary): which icons exist, what they are called, which weights are allowed and how they are brought into Figma. A project uses Phosphor or Lucide, never both. It is not a component: what is painted on screen is Icon.

dos: Look the icon up in icons/phosphor/catalog.json (all of Phosphor) by name, tags or category. If you cannot find it by name, search by tags: "search" is not a name, but it is a tag of magnifying-glass.
To use it in code, first add it to icons/phosphor/registry.json with its `use` field. The catalog is what exists; the registry is what is approved.
Use the regular weight by default. Reserve fill for the active or selected state of the same icon (marked favorite, current tab).

In Figma, always insert the "Phosphor Icon" component: in its properties you choose the icon (Icon, with search over the whole catalog) and the weight (Weight). Do not insert the loose component sets, do not draw icons by hand or paste SVGs.
One icon, one meaning: do not use the same icon for two different actions on the same screen.

donts.case: Using a Phosphor icon that is not in icons/phosphor/registry.json
donts.useInstead: Add it to the registry (with its `use`) and regenerate icons.ts
donts.why: The closed list avoids duplicate or contradictory icons and keeps the bundle small.

donts.case: Mixing Phosphor and Lucide icons in the same project
donts.useInstead: Choose one library per project and look for the equivalent in it
donts.why: Each library has its own grid, thickness and endings; mixing them is noticeable.

donts.case: Using the thin, light, bold or duotone weights
donts.why: Two weights are enough to tell rest from active; more weights break visual consistency.

donts.case: Using fill only to highlight an icon without it changing state
donts.useInstead: The parent component's color or size
donts.why: Fill communicates "active / selected"; using it as decoration confuses that meaning.

donts.case: A lone icon, with no text, for something important
donts.useInstead: Icon plus text, or IconButton with aria-label
donts.why: The meaning of a lone icon is not universal and a screen reader does not announce it.

donts.case: Resizing or recoloring the icon by hand inside a component
donts.useInstead: The size and color of the parent component (Button, IconButton, TextField)
donts.why: The parent already sets them with tokens; a local adjustment breaks consistency.

related.difference: Lucide library: 2 px stroke at 24 × 24 and a single weight. One of the two is chosen per project.
Icon draws an icon from this library on screen with size and accessibility.
Button whose only content is an icon; requires aria-label.

props.name: name
props.description: Icon name in kebab-case, as it appears in icons/phosphor/catalog.json (`magnifying-glass`). In the registry and in icons.ts, the same name in PascalCase (`MagnifyingGlass`); the package exports it with a suffix (`MagnifyingGlassIcon`) and icons.ts re-exports it without it. In Figma, the "Icon" property of the "Phosphor Icon" component, which points to the "Category / magnifying-glass" component set.

props.name: weight
props.description: regular: normal state. fill: the same icon in active or selected state. The other Phosphor weights are not used. In Figma it is the Weight variant of each component set; in "Phosphor Icon" it appears in the panel thanks to "Expose nested instances" and is preserved when changing icon.

root.description: Canvas with viewBox 0 0 256 256 (16 px design grid). Scaled to the size set by the parent.

glyph.description: Figma only: the instance of the chosen icon inside "Phosphor Icon". Swapped with the Icon property and exposes its Weight variant.
glyph.figmaLayer: icon (instancia de «Categoría / nombre», variante Weight=Regular o Weight=Fill)

shape.description: Icon shapes, always filled (also in regular: the stroke is already converted to an outline). Color inherited from the text (currentColor in code; color variable in Figma).

a11y.role: None by default: decorative (aria-hidden). With `label`, role="img" and aria-label.
a11y.name: Provided by the Icon component (label prop), not by the library.
a11y.focusIndicator: Does not receive focus: not interactive.
a11y.minTarget: Does not apply to the icon; if it is inside a button, the press target is the button's.
a11y.contrastNote: An icon with meaning needs ≥ 3:1 against the background (WCAG 1.4.11). It inherits the parent's color: check it there. The regular → fill change cannot be the only signal of a state: accompany it with aria-pressed / aria-selected or text.

canvas.note: Phosphor is designed on a 16 × 16 grid (256 viewBox). In regular the stroke is 16 units: 1 px at 16 px, 1.25 px at 20 px.

renderSizes.note: Same as with Lucide; set by the parent component (see Icon.contract.json).

figmaComponentSize.note: Each variant is created at 24 × 24 in Figma, like the Lucide icons, so that the instance swap between libraries does not change component sizes.

weights.rule: fill only for the active or selected state of the same icon. check.mjs fails if the registry declares a weight that does not exist in the catalog.

fields: pascal (PascalCase, without the package's Icon suffix)
catalog.rule: Never edited by hand. To update to a new Phosphor version: `npm run phosphor:catalog -- --update`.

registry.rule: Subset of the catalog approved for code. check.mjs fails if a registry name does not exist in the catalog and warns if it is an old alias.

code.generatedBy: npm run phosphor:build (in the project: node design-system/scripts/build-phosphor-icons.mjs src/components/icon/icons.ts)
code.import: From the /ssr submodule: no React Context, works in Server and Client Components. IconContext is not used.
code.naming: icons.ts re-exports ArrowRightIcon as ArrowRight: the same name it would have with Lucide, if it exists in both libraries.
code.types: PhosphorIcon (type of the icon component) and IconWeight, re-exported from icons.ts.
code.nextConfig: Optional: add @phosphor-icons/react to experimental.optimizePackageImports in next.config.

figma.order: First the batch-NNN.js batches (create the icons); finally entry.js (creates or updates "Phosphor Icon"). entry.js can be repeated each time icons are added.

entryComponent.name: Phosphor Icon
entryComponent.size: 24 × 24; the inner icon scales with the component

properties.Icon: INSTANCE_SWAP. Default: the first icon in the registry. Preferred values: the icons in icons/phosphor/registry.json (they appear first in the picker); the swap search gives access to the whole catalog.
properties.Weight: Not declared on "Phosphor Icon": it is the inner icon's variant, visible in the panel with "Expose nested instances".

entryComponent.swapRule: All component sets have the same Weight property with the same values (Regular, Fill). That is why, when changing icon, Figma keeps the chosen weight.
entryComponent.use: It is the only thing inserted into designs and inside other components (Button, IconButton, TextField…).

figma.componentName: figmaCategory title / name in kebab-case (component set)
figma.componentDescription: First line `phosphor:name` (used to recognize and avoid duplicates); then categories and tags, so Figma's search finds them.
figma.idempotent: Repeating a batch does not duplicate: it skips icons that already exist.

needsReview: Icon.contract.json is written for Lucide: its `icon` prop is of type LucideIcon and has no `weight`. To use fill through Icon, its version must be bumped (minor) and the prop `weight: 'regular' | 'fill'` added, with type PhosphorIcon in projects that use this library.
The Figma code (scripts/build-phosphor-figma.mjs) was not tested in a real file. Test first with `npm run phosphor:figma` (the registry icons) before running --all.
Check in the real file that, when changing the icon of "Phosphor Icon", Figma keeps the chosen Weight and that the Weight property shows in the panel (Expose nested instances).
For the icons to appear in the swap from other files the library must be published; the preferred values only cover the registry, the rest is found with the search.
The fill variable (colors.neutral.neutral.12) is an assumption, same as in Lucide. If it is not found, icons stay black and the script warns about it.
The names with suffix (ArrowRightIcon) and the /ssr submodule come from the @phosphor-icons/react documentation; a project with the generated icons.ts was not compiled.
The Figma group is Phosphor's figma_category (one per icon); the website categories (there can be several) go in the component description.
Equivalences with the Lucide registry chosen by hand: ChevronDown → CaretDown, EyeOff → EyeSlash, Search → MagnifyingGlass, Trash2 → Trash.
The regular stroke (1 px at 16 px) is thinner than Lucide's (1.33 px). Compare on screen before choosing a library.
The registry icons' uses (`use`) are guidance; they do not come from Phosphor.
